motion.1.note: Skeleton loaders on every list and table.

motion.10.note: Account menu has Follow device / Reduce motion / Full motion; it also respects the device setting.

motion.2.note: Short fade and slide transitions on dialogs, toasts and panels. No full page transitions.

motion.3.note: Planned with the route map in Phase 2.

motion.4.note: Vehicle markers glide to each new fix (lib/glide.ts).

motion.6.note: Buttons press, switches slide, menus fade.

motion.8.note: Planned with the driver app in Phase 4.

nav.1.note: Collapsible side menu; becomes a drawer on phones.

nav.10.note: Home dashboard with drag-and-drop widgets arrives with dashboards in Phase 3.

nav.3.note: Searches vehicles, drivers, routes and stops. Customers join when customer records are added.

nav.5.note: History and route pages: list on the left, map on the right.

nav.6.note: Drag the divider (or use the arrow keys); the width is remembered.

nav.7.note: Pin any page; pins show in the menu and in the palette.

nav.8.note: ? opens the cheat sheet; g then l/r/p jumps; T switches theme; [ collapses the menu.

nav.9.note: Tables save named views (sort, filters, columns, grouping). Custom tabs are not built.

polish.1.note: Empty states say what to do next.

polish.10.note: Five-step product tour and a getting-started checklist for owners and admins.

polish.11.note: Tooltips and a What's new panel.

polish.2.note: Plain-language error states with a retry button and a separate "no access" state.

polish.3.note: Undo for deleting a stop (toast with Undo). Other deletes and edits get it as their screens are built.

polish.4.note: Double-click a cell to edit (people names).

polish.5.note: Sort, filter, group, pin, hide and resize columns, CSV export, saved views.

polish.6.note: Sticky headers; lists over 150 rows are windowed.

polish.8.note: Keyboard use, labels and focus are in place; axe found no contrast problems in the three themes. Not tested with a real screen reader.

polish.9.note: English and French complete. Punjabi and Arabic cover sign-in, navigation and the driver app; Arabic mirrors the layout. Both were drafted without a native reviewer.

report.14.note: Audit log page with filters and CSV export.

security.2.note: Append-only audit log of every change with who, what, when and IP; the app role cannot edit or delete it.

style.1.note: Tokens and components follow a clean, minimal look (apps/web/src/app/tokens.css).

style.2.note: Bento dashboard cards arrive with the dashboards in Phase 3.

style.3.note: Floating map panel uses a light blur; switched off in high-contrast mode.

style.4.note: Dark theme and a dark basemap work. Glowing route lines are not done.

style.5.note: The Playbook says pick one direction and stay with it; soft shadows hurt readability.

style.6.note: Live map fills the page with panels floating on top.

teams.1.note: Owner, admin, dispatcher, manager, driver, customer and read-only. Customer and driver land in their own apps (the customer portal arrives in Phase 4).

teams.2.note: Custom roles with fine-grained permissions (Settings > People & roles).

teams.4.note: Every table is tenant-isolated with Row-Level Security (since Milestone 1); tests prove it.

theme.1.note: Light, dark, follow-the-device and high-contrast themes; picked from the account menu or with the T key.

theme.2.note: Light, dark, follow-the-device and high-contrast themes; picked from the account menu or with the T key.

theme.3.note: Light, dark, follow-the-device and high-contrast themes; picked from the account menu or with the T key.

theme.4.note: Light, dark, follow-the-device and high-contrast themes; picked from the account menu or with the T key.

theme.5.note: Each company sets a brand color and logo in Settings. The color is adjusted so text stays readable (tests in lib/color.test.ts).

theme.6.note: Okabe-Ito palette in --chart-1 to --chart-8, used by every chart.

theme.7.note: The palette exists; route lines on maps adopt it in Phase 2.

route.1.note: Drag stops to reorder on the route page (keyboard works too). apps/web/src/app/(app)/routes/[id].

route.2.note: Optimizer for shortest time or distance (cheapest insertion + 2-opt/or-opt), unit-tested. Uses real road times when a routing engine is set (ROUTING_URL); otherwise straight-line estimates, and the screen says so.

route.3.note: Time windows per stop, treated as hard limits by the optimizer and flagged when late.

route.4.note: Weight, volume and item limits per vehicle; over-capacity is flagged on the board and respected by auto-assign.

route.5.note: Max shift length and mandatory breaks per driver; the optimizer inserts breaks.

route.6.note: Predicted ETAs use hourly speed patterns learned from your own vehicles' positions. Live traffic needs an outside traffic data source.

route.7.note: Avoid tolls, highways, ferries and unpaved roads are sent to the routing engine (OSRM or Valhalla). Enforcing them needs a routing engine; not run in the sandbox.

route.8.note: Height, weight and hazmat limits are sent to Valhalla's truck profile. Needs a Valhalla server; tested only against a stub.

route.9.note: Planner tracks battery range and adds charging stops. Real charger locations need an outside data source, so charge points are entered by you.

route.10.note: Save any route as a template; create routes from templates.

route.11.note: Daily, weekly and custom repeats; the scheduler creates each day's routes once (no duplicates).

route.12.note: CSV import of jobs, with errors listed by row. Excel files are not read directly: save as CSV first.

route.13.note: Address search with saved places and 'did you mean' fixes. Live address lookup needs a geocoding service (Nominatim or similar); tested only against a stub.

route.14.note: Current order vs optimized order shown side by side with cost, time and late stops.

route.15.note: Drop a pin and see where an extra stop fits and what becomes late, before saving.

dispatch.1.note: Dispatch board: unassigned jobs and one lane per driver; drag a job onto a lane or use the menu.

dispatch.2.note: Auto-assign suggests the best driver by skills, capacity, shift and distance, then applies on one click.

dispatch.3.note: Pickup, delivery, service call and inspection jobs.

dispatch.4.note: Low to urgent priority; the rush button inserts an urgent job and says what it delays.

dispatch.5.note: Reassign from the board or the job panel; the driver's route updates and the change is logged.

dispatch.6.note: Unassigned, assigned, started, arrived, done, failed; stop changes update the job automatically.

dispatch.7.note: Photo and signature (earlier milestone) plus package-code scans. Camera scanning needs a browser with BarcodeDetector (Chrome on Android); typing the code works everywhere. Not tried on a real phone.

dispatch.8.note: Notes, tags and file attachments on jobs.

dispatch.9.note: Cancel and reschedule ask for a reason code; history is kept.

dispatch.10.note: Select stops to split onto a new route, or merge another route in.

live.2.note: Trail on the map and day-by-day replay (milestone 3).

live.3.note: Draw circle or polygon zones on a map; enter and exit events are recorded as vehicles move. Sending them out as alerts comes with Phase 4 alerts.

live.4.note: ETAs refresh as vehicles move. They react to real traffic only once a live traffic source is connected.

live.5.note: Moving, idle, stopped and offline colours.

live.7.note: Heat layers for stops, late deliveries and speeding on the live map.

live.8.note: Street and satellite switch, plus a Street View link.

live.9.note: Weather at a vehicle and at each stop's arrival time, from Open-Meteo. Needs internet access to that service; tested only against a stub.

live.10.note: Expiring, revocable share links with a public tracking page. It shows no driver name or plate and is rate-limited.

fleet.1.note: Vehicle records with photo, plate, VIN, capacity, fuel type, EV range and more.

fleet.2.note: Driver profiles: licence, emergency contact, shift limits, skills, training; documents attach to drivers too.

fleet.3.note: Document and licence expiry reminders on the Maintenance page. Emailing them out comes with Phase 4 alerts.

fleet.4.note: Maintenance plans by days or kilometres, due and overdue state, mark-done history.

fleet.5.note: Fuel logs, fuel economy per vehicle and CSV import of fuel-card statements. Live feeds from card companies need their accounts.

fleet.6.note: Trailers and equipment with status and assignment.

fleet.7.note: Check-out and check-in checklist in the driver app; a failed item records a defect and shows in reminders.

fleet.8.note: Incident reports from the driver app with location and photos, tracked from open to closed on the office side.

fleet.9.note: Depot records with parking spots; live occupancy is calculated by the API but not shown in the screens yet.

fleet.10.note: Trip log from vehicle movement with business or personal tags and CSV export.
